summary: Richard P. Boyle earned a PhD from Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and studied under Joshu Sasaki. He taught at UCLA, served as associate professor at Oregon Health & Science University (1986–2000), and was affiliated with the University of New Mexico.

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at McGill University (1988–2003) and the University of New Mexico (2003–2013).

Richard Payne works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held affiliations with the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center.
Richard Peter Hottelet was active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1971.

Richard Phené Spiers (1838–1916) was an architectural scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at King's College London from circa 1856 to 1858 and at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel (1849–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).
Richard Polenberg (1937–2020) was a historian of America who completed his PhD at Columbia University. He served as a professor of American history at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011.

Richard S. Cohen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Luis Oscar Gómez and Walter M. Spink, and he served as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.
Richard Schechner studied at Cornell, Iowa, and Tulane. Since circa 1967, he has served as University Professor at the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University.

Richard Scherzl (b. 1850) was a linguist who studied at Charles University, Saint Petersburg, and Kharkiv. He served as director at Odesa University (1886) and held docent and professorial posts at the University of Kharkiv between 1882 and 1894.

Richard Schmidt (1866–1939) was an Indologist who completed his PhD and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He was librarian for the DMG and later held ordinary and extraordinary professorships at Münster from 1910.

Richard Shilleto (1809–1876) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at Repton School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 1828–1832), and later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Richard Simon (1865–1934) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel. He spent his career at the University of Munich, serving as Privatdozent from 1892 and extraordinary professor from 1906.

Richard Sorabji (b. 1934) is a philosopher and Indologist educated at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held faculty posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

Richard Sproat is a computational linguist who earned his PhD from MIT. His career includes positions at Bell Labs, AT&T Labs, University of Illinois, Oregon Health & Science University, Google, and Sakana AI.
Richard Stothert (1833–1898) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh. He served as principal of Wilson College in Mumbai from 1876 to 1884.

Richard Sylvan (1935–1996) was a philosopher educated at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney (circa 1963–1964) and the Australian National University as a fellow in 1971.

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, he served there as Associate Director of Research Development and taught at Smith College as a visiting lecturer.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who earned a Sanskrit doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and Field Museum president.

Richard Wilhelm (1873–1930) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen. He served as guest professor at Peking University (1923) and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924.
